d.name: Precision Health
d.logic: Calendar-led patient orientation; neutral vertical navigation; fine rules and compact parallel clinical panes.
d.risk: A disciplined grid can feel impersonal. Test warmth through readable language and patient hierarchy rather than extra decoration.

e.name: Human Clinical
e.logic: Open horizontal navigation; asymmetric patient composition; one deep-green appointment anchor; quiet, generously spaced clinical sections.
e.risk: The softer rhythm costs vertical space. Dense clinician information must retain explicit grouping and strong local navigation.

f.name: Next-Gen Health OS
f.logic: Graphite horizontal workspace; a luminous appointment band; flat divided clinical panes; cyan used only for orientation and action.
f.type: IBM Plex Sans + Noto Sans Arabic
f.risk: A dark workspace can feel technical and needs real-device glare testing. “OS” is a review label, never a claim of complete health coverage.
